4448.new_note: *And fear not them which kill the body, but are not able to kill the soul: but rather fear him which is able to destroy both soul and body in hell.* (Matthew 10:28) *And when he had bravely met his glorious death, the third son was brought forward and was earnestly entreated by many to taste and so to save himself. But he answered in a loud voice, ‘Are ye ignorant that the same father begat me and my brothers that are dead, and the same mother gave us birth, and in the same doctrines was I brought up? I do not forswear the noble bond of brotherhood. Therefore if ye have any engine of torment, apply it to this body of mine; for my soul ye cannot reach, not if ye would.’ But they were greatly angered at the bold speech of the man, and they dislocated his hands and his feet with their dislocating engines, and wrenched his limbs out of their sockets, and unstrung them; and they twisted round his fingers, and his arms, and his legs, and his elbow-joints. And in no wise being able to strangle his spirit they stripped off his skin, taking the points of the fingers with it, and tore in Scythian fashion the scalp from his head, and straightway brought him to the wheel. And on this they twisted his spine till he saw his own flesh hanging in strips and great gouts of blood pouring down from his entrails. And at the point of death he said, ‘We, O most abominable tyrant, suffer thus for our upbringing and our virtue that are of Elohim (God); but thou for thy impiety and thy cruelty shalt endure torments without end.’* (4 Maccabees 10:1) The Messiah (Christ) tells his own that those who kill the body cannot kill the soul, and that the fear belongs to the One who holds both. The third of the seven brothers says the same thing to Antiochus on the wheel: apply every engine to this body, for my soul you cannot reach. He is of the seed of Yahudah (Judah), dying for keeping the Law of his fathers, and he tells the tyrant that his own cruelty will meet torments without end. The persecutor's power stops at the body, and the soul is held in another hand.
4448.member_note: 4 Maccabees 10:1 — *apply it to this body of mine; for my soul ye cannot reach, not if ye would.* The third brother tells Antiochus what Yahusha (Jesus) later tells his own, that the soul is beyond the persecutor's reach.

4449.new_note: *And fear not them which kill the body, but are not able to kill the soul: but rather fear him which is able to destroy both soul and body in hell.* (Matthew 10:28) *O Reason of the sons, lord over the passions! O religion, that wast dearer to the mother than her children! The mother, having two choices before her, religion and the present saving alive of her seven sons according to the tyrant's promise, loved rather religion, which saveth unto eternal life according to Elohim (God). O how may I express the passionate love of parents for children? We stamp a marvellous likeness of our soul and of our shape on the tender nature of the child, and most of all through the mother's sympathy with her children being deeper than the father's. For women are softer of soul than men, and the more children they bear the more do they abound in love for them.* (4 Maccabees 15:1) The Messiah (Christ) sets the order of fear plainly: do not fear those who can only reach the body, but the One who has power over soul and body. The mother of the seven brothers had that choice laid before her in the flesh, her sons' lives saved for the present on the tyrant's word, or religion which saves unto eternal life according to Elohim (God). She loved religion more, and she and her sons kept the Law of Yahuah (God) unto death. It is the same priority the Messiah (Christ) gives his own when he sends them out to be hated.
4449.member_note: 4 Maccabees 15:1 — *loved rather religion, which saveth unto eternal life according to Elohim (God).* The mother chooses eternal life over the saving alive of her sons, the same order of fear Matthew 10:28 gives.

4450.new_note: *And ye shall be hated of all men for my name’s sake: but he that endureth to the end shall be saved.* (Matthew 10:22) *For on that day virtue, proving them through endurance, set before them the prize of victory in incorruption in everlasting life.* (4 Maccabees 17:12) The Messiah (Christ) tells his own they will be hated of all men for his name, and that salvation belongs to the one who endures to the end. The book says of the seven brothers, Eleazar and their mother that on the day of trial virtue proved them through endurance and set before them the prize of victory in incorruption and everlasting life. Both put endurance first and the prize after it. These were the seed of Yahudah (Judah) holding to the Law unto death, and the life held out to them is life that does not decay, which the faithful asleep await with us at the resurrection.
4450.member_note: 4 Maccabees 17:12 — *virtue, proving them through endurance, set before them the prize of victory in incorruption in everlasting life.* Endurance is proved first and the prize of incorruption follows, as Matthew 10:22 says of the one who endures to the end.

4451.new_note: *And ye shall be hated of all men for my name’s sake: but he that endureth to the end shall be saved.* (Matthew 10:22) *The tyrant himself and his whole council admired their endurance, whereby they now do both stand beside the throne of Elohim (God) and live the blessed age.* (4 Maccabees 17:17) The Messiah (Christ) tells his own they will be hated of all men and that the one who endures to the end shall be saved. The book gives the seven brothers as the picture of that endurance: even the tyrant and his council admired it, and the book says it has brought them to stand beside the throne of Elohim (God) and live the blessed age. Endurance in the Law of their fathers did not end in the grave. The faithful who have fallen asleep wait with us for the first resurrection and are not made perfect without us, so what the verse holds out is the end promised to the one who endures.
4451.member_note: 4 Maccabees 17:17 — *they now do both stand beside the throne of Elohim (God) and live the blessed age.* The brothers' endurance is shown as ending beside the throne of Elohim (God), the end Matthew 10:22 promises.

4452.new_note: *For it is not ye that speak, but the Spirit of your Father which speaketh in you.* (Matthew 10:20) *But he said, ‘Even if thou dost remove my organ of speech, Elohim (God) is a hearer also of the speechless.* (4 Maccabees 10:4) The Messiah (Christ) tells his own not to take thought how or what they shall speak when they are brought before rulers, because the Spirit of their Father speaks in them. The fourth of the seven brothers faces the same hour when Antiochus orders his tongue cut out, and he answers that Elohim (God) is a hearer also of the speechless. What matters in the hour of trial does not depend on a prepared speech or even on the tongue, since the Father hears and is present with the one who stands for his Law.
4452.member_note: 4 Maccabees 10:4 — *Even if thou dost remove my organ of speech, Elohim (God) is a hearer also of the speechless.* The brother whose tongue is to be cut out trusts that Elohim (God) hears without words, as Matthew 10:20 promises the Father's Spirit speaks in his own.

4858.new_note: *And he went a little further, and fell on his face, and prayed, saying, O my Father, if it be possible, let this cup pass from me: nevertheless not as I will, but as thou wilt.* (Matthew 26:39) *'Why dost thou delay, O tyrant? We are ready to die rather than transgress the commandments of our fathers.* (4 Maccabees 9:1) Both stand before a death they could avoid and choose the will of Elohim (God) over their own preservation. The seven brothers, the seed of Yahudah (Judah), tell the tyrant they are ready to die rather than transgress the commandments of their fathers, so they witness that Torah stands to the death. The Messiah (Christ) in the garden prays that the cup pass from him and then gives himself to the Father's will, nevertheless not as I will, but as thou wilt. The brothers' endurance foreshadows his laying down of his life, though the cup he takes is far greater than their pain, for he drinks it as the Pesach (Passover) lamb in obedience to the Father.
4858.member_note: 4 Maccabees 9:1 — *We are ready to die rather than transgress the commandments of our fathers.* The brothers' readiness to die rather than break the Law foreshadows the Messiah's (Christ's) submission to the Father's will in the garden.

4859.new_note: *He went away again the second time, and prayed, saying, O my Father, if this cup may not pass away from me, except I drink it, thy will be done.* (Matthew 26:42) *And righteousness won the victory, and gave the crown to her athletes.* (4 Maccabees 17:15) The Messiah (Christ) prays a second time that if the cup cannot pass he will drink it, and he ends with thy will be done, the Son's willing submission to the Father who sent him. The book says of the seven brothers that righteousness won the victory and gave the crown to her athletes, because they would not turn from the Law even to save their lives. Their crown is the foreshadow, and his drinking of the cup leads to the resurrection on the third day. Obedience to the Father's will through death is the road to the prize in both.
4859.member_note: 4 Maccabees 17:15 — *righteousness won the victory, and gave the crown to her athletes.* The brothers' crown for faithfulness unto death foreshadows the Messiah's (Christ's) obedience, thy will be done, that leads to the third day.

4860.new_note: *Rise, let us be going: behold, he is at hand that doth betray me.* (Matthew 26:46) *And these men, therefore, having sanctified themselves for Elohim's (God’s) sake, not only have received this honour, but also the honour that through them the enemy had no more power over our people, and the tyrant suffered punishment, and our country was purified, they having as it were become a ransom for our nation’s sin; and through the blood of these righteous men and the propitiation of their death, the divine Providence delivered Yashar'el (Israel) that before was evil entreated.* (4 Maccabees 17:19) The Messiah (Christ) rises from his prayer and walks toward the one who betrays him, not away from him, because the hour of his laying down his life is at hand. The book, in its own voice, says of the seven brothers that they became as it were a ransom for the nation's sin, and that through their death the divine Providence delivered Yashar'el (Israel). That is the book's witness, and it foreshadows the Messiah's (Christ's) laying down of his life rather than replacing it, for the brothers show that Torah stands to the death. The cross is the door home to the commandments, and the Messiah (Christ) goes to it willingly as the Pesach (Passover) lamb.

4874.new_note: *He trusted in Elohim (God); let him deliver him now, if he will have him: for he said, I am the Son of Elohim (God).* (Matthew 27:43) *But as many as with their whole heart make righteousness their first thought, these alone are able to master the weakness of the flesh, believing that unto Elohim (God) they die not, as our patriarchs, Abraham and Isaac and Jacob, died not, but that they live unto Elohim (God).* (4 Maccabees 7:12) The mockers say that since he trusted in Elohim (God), let him deliver him now. The book answers from the other side: those who make righteousness their first thought believe that they die not unto Elohim (God), as Abraham, Isaac and Jacob died and yet live unto him. Deliverance for the one who trusts is not measured by whether he comes down from the cross. The fathers sleep and await the first resurrection with us, and Yahusha's (Jesus's) deliverance came on the third day.
4874.member_note: 4 Maccabees 7:12 — *believing that unto Elohim (God) they die not, as our patriarchs, Abraham and Isaac and Jacob, died not.* Those who trust Elohim (God) live unto him even through death, which answers the mockers' demand for deliverance now.

63407.new_note: Leviticus 19:9 — *And when ye reap the harvest of your land, thou shalt not wholly reap the corners of thy field, neither shalt thou gather the gleanings of thy harvest.* To be one who "refrains from gleaning his stubbles" is to obey the law of the corners and the gleanings left for the poor.
63407.flag: Quote now matches live 4 Maccabees 2:2 wording ('refrains from gleaning his stubbles').

63464.new_note: Hebrews 9:14 — *the blood of Messiah (Christ), who through the eternal Spirit offered himself without spot to Elohim (God), purge your conscience from dead works* — the blood that truly purifies, which Eleazar's *make my blood their purification* pointed toward.

63469.new_note: Isaiah 53:10 — *when thou shalt make his soul an offering for sin, he shall see his seed, he shall prolong his days* — the soul given as an offering for sin, which the martyr's surrendered soul only pointed toward.

63470.new_note: Isaiah 53:5 — *he was wounded for our transgressions, he was bruised for our iniquities: the chastisement of our peace was upon him; and with his stripes we are healed* — the Suffering Servant whose pattern Eleazar's blood-plea dimly reflects, a pattern that waited for its fulfilment.

63517.new_note: Matthew 10:18 — *And ye shall be brought before governors and kings for my sake, for a testimony against them and the Gentiles.* The youth confessing before the tyrant that he suffers for defending the Law of Elohim is the standing before kings as a testimony that the Messiah foretold.

63524.new_note: Deuteronomy 30:16 — *I command thee this day to love Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God), to walk in his ways, and to keep his commandments and his statutes and his judgments, that thou mayest live and multiply.* Their resolve to walk in obedience to the Law and take Moses as counsellor is the walking in his ways that Moses commanded for life.

63552.new_note: 1 John 3:16 — *Hereby perceive we the love of Elohim (God), because he laid down his life for us: and we ought to lay down our lives for the brethren* — the laying down of life for one's brethren that the seven enacted to the death, brotherly love bred under the Law.

63607.new_note: 2 Timothy 4:8 — *Henceforth there is laid up for me a crown of righteousness, which Yahusha (Lord), the righteous judge, shall give me at that day: and not to me only, but unto all them also that love his appearing.* — the crown of righteousness given by the Judge, as righteousness *gave the crown to her athletes.*

63619.new_note: Isaiah 53:5 — *But he was wounded for our transgressions, he was bruised for our iniquities: the chastisement of our peace was upon him; and with his stripes we are healed* — the Suffering Servant whose wounded blood truly delivers, which the martyrs' death only pointed toward.

63622.new_note: Isaiah 53:12 — *he hath poured out his soul unto death... and he bare the sin of many, and made intercession for the transgressors* — the One who pours out his soul and bears the nation's sin, the one whom the martyrs' blood foreshadows.

63625.new_note: Hebrews 9:14 — *the blood of Messiah, who through the eternal Spirit offered himself without spot to Elohim, purge your conscience from dead works* — the blood that truly cleanses the people, which the martyrs' blood only pointed toward.

63655.new_note: Daniel 12:2 — *and many of them that sleep in the dust of the earth shall awake, some to everlasting life* — the resurrection of the just, the *pure and immortal souls* the sons of Abraham received from Elohim.

69292.new_note: Genesis 4:2 — *And she again bare his brother Abel. And Abel was a keeper of sheep, but Cain was a tiller of the ground.* The two sons Eve bears in Adam and Eve 1:1, Cain and Abel, are the same pair Moses names in their birth order.

69295.new_note: 1 John 3:12 — *Not as Cain, who was of that wicked one, and slew his brother. And wherefore slew he him? Because his own works were evil, and his brother's righteous.* The hand of Cain in Adam and Eve 3:1 is the very fratricide John sets as the warning against hatred.

69296.new_note: Hebrews 11:4 — *By faith Abel offered unto Elohim (God) a more excellent sacrifice than Cain, by which he obtained witness that he was righteous, Elohim (God) testifying of his gifts: and by it he being dead yet speaketh.* The murdered Abel of Adam and Eve 3:1 is the righteous one whose blood still speaks.

69298.new_note: Genesis 4:8 — *And Cain talked with Abel his brother: and it came to pass, when they were in the field, that Cain rose up against Abel his brother, and slew him.* Abel found murdered by his brother's hand in Adam and Eve 3:1 is the slaying Moses records in the field.

69301.new_note: Genesis 5:3 — *And Adam lived an hundred and thirty years, and begat a son in his own likeness, after his image; and called his name Seth.* The Seth born to Adam in Adam and Eve 4:1 is the son begotten in Adam's own likeness who heads the book of the generations.

69302.new_note: Genesis 4:25 — *And Adam knew his wife again; and she bare a son, and called his name Seth: For Elohim (God), said she, hath appointed me another seed instead of Abel, whom Cain slew.* Adam's word in Adam and Eve 4:1, a son in place of Abel whom Cain slew, is Moses' account verbatim of the appointed seed.

69304.new_note: Genesis 5:5 — *And all the days that Adam lived were nine hundred and thirty years: and he died.* The nine hundred and thirty years and the sickness unto death in Adam and Eve 5:1 are the exact span Moses sets down for the first man.

69306.new_note: Genesis 2:17 — *But of the tree of the knowledge of good and evil, thou shalt not eat of it: for in the day that thou eatest thereof thou shalt surely die.* The one tree forbidden and the death through it in Adam and Eve 7:1 are the single command and its sentence Moses set down.

69308.new_note: Psalms 139:12 — *Yea, the darkness hideth not from thee; but the night shineth as the day: the darkness and the light are both alike to thee.* The house cannot hide from its builder, says Adam and Eve 8:1; no darkness hides the creature from the Maker, says the psalm.

69310.new_note: Genesis 3:9 — *And Yahuah Elohim (the LORD God) called unto Adam, and said unto him, Where art thou?* The terrible call "Adam, where art thou" in Adam and Eve 8:1 is the very word Moses records first after the Fall.

69311.new_note: Genesis 3:8 — *And they heard the voice of Yahuah Elohim (the LORD God) walking in the garden in the cool of the day: and Adam and his wife hid themselves from the presence of Yahuah Elohim (the LORD God) amongst the trees of the garden.* Yahuah coming into paradise and the man hiding in Adam and Eve 8:1 is Moses' scene of the voice in the garden.

69314.new_note: Genesis 3:17 — *And unto Adam he said, Because thou hast hearkened unto the voice of thy wife, and hast eaten of the tree, of which I commanded thee, saying, Thou shalt not eat of it: cursed is the ground for thy sake; in sorrow shalt thou eat of it all the days of thy life.* Adam's distress and toils in Adam and Eve 9:1 are the sorrow Moses laid on the man for hearkening to his wife.

69319.new_note: Genesis 9:2 — *And the fear of you and the dread of you shall be upon every beast of the earth, and upon every fowl of the air... into your hand are they delivered.* The subjection of the beasts, fractured in Eden so that the beast now "fights with the image of Elohim," is the dominion renewed to Noah.

69320.new_note: Genesis 1:28 — *And Elohim (God) blessed them... and have dominion over the fish of the sea, and over the fowl of the air, and over every living thing that moveth upon the earth.* The plea that the beast "was made subject to the image of Elohim" recalls the dominion granted at creation.

69336.new_note: James 1:15 — *Then when lust hath conceived, it bringeth forth sin: and sin, when it is finished, bringeth forth death.* James spells out the chain Adam and Eve 19:1 names lust 'the root and beginning of every sin' that ends in death.

69339.new_note: Genesis 3:7 — *And the eyes of them both were opened, and they knew that they were naked; and they sewed fig leaves together, and made themselves aprons.* Eve's eyes opened and her flight to leaves (Adam and Eve 20:1,4-5, the fig tree alone) is this very verse told from within.

69342.new_note: 1 Thessalonians 4:16 — *For Yahusha (Lord) himself shall descend from heaven with a shout, with the voice of the archangel, and with the trump of Elohim (God): and the dead in Messiah (Christ) shall rise first:* The archangel and trumpet heralding Yahuah's coming in Eden is the same figure Paul uses for the descent at the last day.

69345.new_note: Genesis 3:8 — *And they heard the voice of Yahuah Elohim (the LORD God) walking in the garden in the cool of the day: and Adam and his wife hid themselves from the presence of Yahuah Elohim (the LORD God) amongst the trees of the garden.* Elohim's appearing in paradise to judge Adam (Adam and Eve 22:1–2) is this coming of Yahuah into the garden, dramatised with trumpet and chariot.

69352.new_note: Genesis 3:17 — *And unto Adam he said, Because thou hast hearkened unto the voice of thy wife, and hast eaten of the tree, of which I commanded thee, saying, Thou shalt not eat of it: cursed is the ground for thy sake; in sorrow shalt thou eat of it all the days of thy life;* The 'hearkened to thy wife' and 'cursed is the earth' of Adam and Eve 24:1 is this verse.

69358.new_note: Revelation 12:9 — *And the great dragon was cast out, that old serpent, called the Devil, and Satan, which deceiveth the whole world: he was cast out into the earth, and his angels were cast out with him.* 'That old serpent' is the same enemy of Adam and Eve 26:2, his head now bruised by being cast down.

69383.new_note: Revelation 6:12 — *And I beheld when he had opened the sixth seal, and, lo, there was a great earthquake; and the sun became black as sackcloth of hair, and the moon became as blood.* The hidden light of the luminaries is John's sun turned black as sackcloth and blood-red moon at the great judgment.
69383.flag: | voice: Patched clause reads 'John's sun that turns black as sackcloth, and blood-red moon' — the stray comma and relative clause break the pairing with 'blood-red moon' and the sentence stumbles. Quotation and citation intact.

69405.new_note: 1 Corinthians 15:22 — *For as in Adam all die, even so in Messiah (Christ) shall all be made alive.* Raising Adam with every man of his seed is Paul's word that in Adam all die and in Messiah (Christ) all are made alive — the same root and the same harvest.
69405.flag: | voice: Patched words name the Messiah without the parenthetical: 'in Messiah all are made alive'. Our own prose must read Messiah (Christ). Everything else surgical and clean.

69411.new_note: Ephesians 5:31 — *For this cause shall a man leave his father and mother, and shall be joined unto his wife, and they two shall be one flesh.* Eve's plea that they not be separated is Paul's one-flesh union carried from Genesis.

69433.new_note: Hebrews 1:6 — *And again, when he bringeth in the firstbegotten into the world, he saith, And let all the angels of Elohim (God) worship him.* The command that Michael and the angels worship the image of Elohim in Adam and Eve 56:1 finds its true end in the firstbegotten, whom all the angels of Elohim are bidden to worship.

69434.new_note: Colossians 1:15 — *Who is the image of the invisible Elohim (God), the firstborn of every creature.* The image of Elohim borne by the formed man in Adam and Eve 56:1 has its perfect pattern in the Son, the true image of the unseen Elohim.

69435.new_note: Genesis 2:7 — *And Yahuah Elohim (the LORD God) formed man of the dust of the ground, and breathed into his nostrils the breath of life; and man became a living soul.* The breath of life the devil says was blown into Adam in Adam and Eve 56:1 is the breath Moses says Yahuah Elohim breathed into the man's nostrils.

69436.new_note: Genesis 1:27 — *So Elohim (God) created man in his own image, in the image of Elohim (God) created he him; male and female created he them.* The image of Elohim that the angels were bidden to honour in Adam and Eve 56:1 is the image Moses says was stamped upon the man at his creation.

69438.new_note: 1 Enoch 6:2 — *And the angels, the children of the heaven, saw and lusted after them, and said to one another: 'Come, let us choose us wives from among the children of men and beget us children.'* The angels who rebelled with the adversary in Adam and Eve 58:1 are remembered in the book of the fathers as the Watchers, the children of heaven who forsook their estate.

69439.new_note: Revelation 12:9 — *And the great dragon was cast out, that old serpent, called the Devil, and Satan, which deceiveth the whole world: he was cast out into the earth, and his angels were cast out with him.* The expulsion onto the earth that the devil mourns in Adam and Eve 59:1 is the casting-out of the dragon and his angels into the earth that John saw.

69440.new_note: Revelation 12:7 — *And there was war in heaven: Michael and his angels fought against the dragon; and the dragon fought and his angels.* The banishing of the adversary and his angels from glory in Adam and Eve 59:1 is the war in heaven where Michael and his angels war against the dragon and his.

69441.new_note: Luke 10:18 — *And he said unto them, I beheld Satan as lightning fall from heaven.* The casting-out the devil confesses in Adam and Eve 59:1, that followed his refusal in 57:3, is the lightning-fall the Messiah testifies He beheld.

69442.new_note: Ezekiel 28:17 — *Thine heart was lifted up because of thy beauty, thou hast corrupted thy wisdom by reason of thy brightness: I will cast thee to the ground, I will lay thee before kings, that they may behold thee.* The lifted-up heart that would not bow in Adam and Eve 57:1 is the corruption Ezekiel names in the covering cherub cast to the ground.

69443.new_note: Ezekiel 28:15 — *Thou wast perfect in thy ways from the day that thou wast created, till iniquity was found in thee.* The angels under the adversary who joined his refusal in Adam and Eve 58:1 followed one in whom, as Ezekiel says, iniquity was found after his perfect beginning.

69444.new_note: Isaiah 14:14 — *I will ascend above the heights of the clouds; I will be like the El Elyon (most High).* The devil's last word in Adam and Eve 58:1 — 'I will be like the Highest' — is the very claim Isaiah records, to be like the El Elyon.

69445.new_note: Isaiah 14:13 — *For thou hast said in thine heart, I will ascend into heaven, I will exalt my throne above the stars of Elohim (God): I will sit also upon the mount of the congregation, in the sides of the north.* The boast of Adam and Eve 58:1 — to set his seat above the stars of heaven — is almost word for word the throne Isaiah's fallen one would exalt above the stars of Elohim.

69446.new_note: Isaiah 14:12 — *How art thou fallen from heaven, O Lucifer, son of the morning! how art thou cut down to the ground, which didst weaken the nations!* The adversary's refusal in Adam and Eve 57:1 to honour his junior is the pride Isaiah laments in the one fallen from heaven.

69447.new_note: Romans 5:14 — *Nevertheless death reigned from Adam to Moses, even over them that had not sinned after the similitude of Adam's transgression, who is the figure of him that was to come.* Though Eve takes the blame in Adam and Eve 61:1, Paul fixes the reign of death upon Adam's transgression — and names him the figure of Him that was to come.

69448.new_note: 1 Timothy 2:14 — *And Adam was not deceived, but the woman being deceived was in the transgression.* Eve's confession in Adam and Eve 61:1, 'I have erred and been led astray,' is exactly Paul's account that the woman, being deceived, was in the transgression.

69449.new_note: 1 Timothy 2:13 — *For Adam was first formed, then Eve.* Eve's word in Adam and Eve 61:1, that life is granted to Adam who erred neither first nor second, rests on the order Paul names — Adam first formed, then Eve.

69450.new_note: Genesis 3:6 — *And when the woman saw that the tree was good for food, and that it was pleasant to the eyes, and a tree to be desired to make one wise, she took of the fruit thereof, and did eat, and gave also unto her husband with her; and he did eat.* The error Eve confesses in Adam and Eve 61:1, that she did not keep the commandment, is the taking and eating Moses records of the woman.

69451.new_note: Genesis 4:1 — *And Adam knew Eve his wife; and she conceived, and bare Cain, and said, I have gotten a man from Yahuah (LORD).* The son Eve bears and names Cain in Adam and Eve 64:1 is the very firstborn Moses sets at the head of Adam's generations.

69452.new_note: Genesis 3:16 — *Unto the woman he said, I will greatly multiply thy sorrow and thy conception; in sorrow thou shalt bring forth children; and thy desire shall be to thy husband, and he shall rule over thee.* The distress and pains that overtake Eve at her bearing in Adam and Eve 62:1 are the sorrow in childbearing Moses pronounced upon the woman.

69453.new_note: Genesis 5:4 — *And the days of Adam after he had begotten Seth were eight hundred years: and he begat sons and daughters.* The eight hundred years and the sons and daughters Adam begets after Seth in Adam and Eve 67:2 are the very span and increase Moses records in the generations of Adam.

69454.new_note: Genesis 4:25 — *And Adam knew his wife again; and she bare a son, and called his name Seth: For Elohim (God), said she, hath appointed me another seed instead of Abel, whom Cain slew.* Adam's word in Adam and Eve 67:1, that Seth is begotten in place of Abel whom Cain slew, is the very reckoning Moses sets at Seth's naming.

69455.new_note: 1 John 3:12 — *Not as Cain, who was of that wicked one, and slew his brother. And wherefore slew he him? Because his own works were evil, and his brother's righteous.* The murder told in Adam and Eve 66:2 is the deed John holds up as the pattern of hatred — Cain, of the wicked one, who slew his righteous brother.

69456.new_note: Genesis 4:8 — *And Cain talked with Abel his brother: and it came to pass, when they were in the field, that Cain rose up against Abel his brother, and slew him.* The slaying of Abel by Cain in Adam and Eve 66:2 is the murder in the field Moses records.

69457.new_note: Genesis 4:2 — *And she again bare his brother Abel. And Abel was a keeper of sheep, but Cain was a tiller of the ground.* The two callings made for the brothers in Adam and Eve 66:1, Cain the husbandman and Abel the shepherd, are the very trades Moses assigns them.

69526.new_note: Revelation 14:13 — *And I heard a voice from heaven saying unto me, Write, Blessed are the dead which die in Yahusha (Lord) from henceforth: Yea, saith the Spirit, that they may rest from their labours; and their works do follow them.* The seventh day as the sign of the resurrection is the blessed rest of the dead in Yahuah — labour ended, the age to come begun.
